{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{use mdy dates|date=February 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2009–10 |team=Ohio Bobcats |image=Ohio Bobcats wordmark.svg |image_size=150 |conference=Mid-American Conference |division=East Division |short_conf=MAC |CoachRank= |APRank= |record=22–15 |conf_record=7–9 |head_coach=[[John Groce]] |hc_year = 2nd |asst_coach1=[[Chris Holtmann]] |asst_coach2=Ramon Williams |asst_coach3=[[Dustin Ford]] |stadium=[[Convocation Center (Ohio University)|Convocation Center]] |champion=MAC Tournament Champions |bowl = [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result =Round of 32 }} {{2009–10 Mid-American Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2009–10 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team''' represented [[Ohio University]] in the college basketball season of [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]]. The team was coached by [[John Groce]] and played their homes game at the [[Convocation Center (Ohio University)|Convocation Center]].{{cite web |url=https://www.ohio.edu/building-directory/convocation-center|title=Convocation Center|website=Ohio University|language=en|access-date=2022-09-29}}{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/coaches/john-groce-1.html|title=John Groce|website=Sports Reference|language=en|access-date=2022-09-29}} At the end of the regular season Ohio was seeded 9th in the [[2010 MAC men's basketball tournament]] with a [[2009–10 Mid-American Conference men's basketball season|conference]] record of 7–9. However, the Bobcats reeled off four straight wins to win the [[2010 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]], including an overtime win over [[2009–10 Akron Zips men's basketball team|Akron]] in the championship game. The victory earned them an automatic bid to the [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. On [[Selection Sunday]] they were given the 14 seed in the Midwest region and slated to play the 3 seed [[2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]]. In a huge upset, the Bobcats dominated the Hoyas almost the whole game in the first round of the NCAA tournament, beating them 97–83.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=300770046|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170415202341/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=300770046|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 15, 2017|title=Bobcats upend Hoyas for first tournament win in 27 years|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-05-21}} The win was Ohio's first NCAA Tournament win since 1983, when they toppled Illinois State in the first round. The Bobcats advanced to face the #6 seed [[2009–10 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]]. They were knocked off by Tennessee 83–67 to finish the season 22–15.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=300792633|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220521170335/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=300792633|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 21, 2022|title=Tennessee rolls over Ohio, secures third Sweet 16 in last four years|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-05-21}} ==Before the season== ===Roster changes=== The Ohio Bobcats lost six players from last year's team. Out of those six players, three were starters and two players recorded over 10 points per game. [[Jerome Tillman]], who averaged 17.7 points and 8.1 rebounds per game for the Bobcats, now plays for the French team [[ÉS Chalon-sur-Saône]]{{Cite web |url=http://www.lalsace.fr/fr/sports/article/2039913,219/Les-effectifs.html |title=Les effectifs |language=French |trans-title=Staffing |date=2009-02-10 }}{{Dead link|date=May 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} The other two starters that departed from last year's team were Justin Orr and Michael Allen.
